texts:
One observes with a degree of astonishment
    that the Iberian nation of Spain
        was, in fact, the final bastion of European 
            states to be embroiled in the tumult of 
                internecine strife, specifically a civil war 
                    precipitated by the competing claims 
                        of sundry branches of the royal family 
                            each seeking to assert dominance and 
                                ascendancy to the throne, a lamentable 
                                    spectacle that sorely tested the mettle 
                                        of that fair realm.

It is a most astonishing fact, my dear fellow,
    that the Iberian nation of Spain was the final bastion
        of European countries to succumb to the scourge
            of a fratricidal conflict, a civil war of most dire
                proportions, occasioned by the most distressing
                    circumstances of rival claimants to the throne,
                        each professing a rightful descent from the royal
                            lineage, and thereby emboldened to take up arms
                                against their own kin, in a most lamentable
                                    display of ambition and discord.

Good sir, permit me to remark,
    it is nothing short of astounding to note
       that Spain, a land steeped in tradition and majesty,
          was the last bastion of Europe to be beset
             by the scourge of internecine strife,
                as rival claimants to the throne, all issuing
                   from the very same illustrious royal lineage,
                      did take up arms against one another in a
                         most distressing and lamentable display of
                            fratricidal discord.

It is indeed a most remarkable circumstance
    that the esteemed nation of Spain
        should be the final bastion of continental Europe
            to be embroiled in the turmoil of civil strife
                as a consequence of competing claims to the throne
                    by sundry branches of the royal family, each seeking
                        to assert its legitimacy and ascendancy over the realm.
